To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) model checking can be made scalable by exploiting design structure, (2) the design structure is best represented in a reactive module hierarchy, and (3) the design structure can be exploited in the model checking algorithms by means of compositional reasoning and assume-guarantee reasoning.

(1) the state space of reactive designs can be represented and manipulated in a hierarchical fashion; (2) the hierarchical representation can be used to develop scalable verification algorithms that exploit design structure; (3) the design hierarchy can be exploited to perform compositional verification of requirements; and (4) the design hierarchy is a natural basis for the development of a model checking framework that supports the incremental development of verification algorithms.

(1) the use of hierarchical design structures in model checking leads to significant performance improvements, and (2) the use of a scripting language to implement new verification algorithms leads to a more rapid development of new algorithms and to the ability to easily experiment with different algorithms and different design structures.

developing scalable model checking algorithms and tools that exploit design structure.
